<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>(a) General Development of Business </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Blackstone Multi-Strategy Hedge Fund L.P. (the &#8220;<B>Fund</B>&#8221;) forms a part of BXHF, an investment program designed to offer
eligible individuals and other investors access to Blackstone&#8217;s multi-asset investing division (the &#8220;<B>Multi-Asset Investing Division</B>&#8221; or &#8220;<B>BXMA</B>&#8221;). Our general partner, Blackstone Alternative Asset Management
Associates LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (previously defined as the &#8220;<B>General Partner</B>&#8221;), our investment manager, Blackstone Alternative Asset Management L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (previously defined as the
&#8220;<B>Investment Manager</B>&#8221;), and our <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">sub-investment</FONT> manager, Blackstone Alternative Solutions L.L.C., a Delaware limited liability company (previously defined as the &#8220;<B>Affiliated</B> <B><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Manager</B>&#8221; or &#8220;<B>BAS</B>,&#8221; together with the Investment Manager, the &#8220;<B>BXHF Managers</B>&#8221; and the BXHF Managers together with the General Partner, the
&#8220;<B>Sponsor</B>&#8221;), are affiliates of Blackstone Inc. (&#8220;<B>Blackstone</B>&#8221;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We expect to conduct a continuous
private offering of our Units in reliance on exemptions from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#8220;<B>1933 Act</B>&#8221;), to investors that are both (i)&nbsp;accredited investors (as defined in
Regulation D under the 1933 Act) and (ii)&nbsp;qualified purchasers (as defined in the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the &#8220;<B>1940 Act</B>&#8221;) and rules thereunder). BXHF is structured as a perpetual-life strategy, with
monthly, fully funded subscriptions and periodic redemptions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>(b) [Reserved] </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>(c) Description of Business </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>The Fund &#8212;
Blackstone Multi-Strategy Hedge Fund L.P. </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund, a limited partnership, was formed on October&nbsp;28, 2025 under the laws of the
State of Delaware. We are a private fund exempt from registration under the 1940 Act pursuant to Section&nbsp;3(c)(7) of the 1940 Act. Our investment objective is to generate attractive long term risk-adjusted returns across market cycles. The Fund
aims to balance growth and preservation of capital, and seeks to produce an attractive return with low volatility and low sensitivity to traditional assets such as stocks and bonds. We will seek to meet our investment objective by investing
dynamically in liquid and semi-liquid opportunities across four strategies: credit, equities, special situations and trading (collectively, the &#8220;<B>Investment Strategies</B>&#8221;), each of which is expected to have several underlying <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">sub-strategies.</FONT> The Fund is expected to be well-diversified across the Investment Strategies as well as <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">sub-strategies</FONT> and liquidity horizons. See &#8220;<I>&#8212;Investment
Strategies</I>&#8221; and &#8220;<I>&#8212;Investment Process Overview</I>&#8221; below for information regarding the Fund&#8217;s process for identifying investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of the date of this Registration Statement, we have not yet commenced investment operations and activities and, as a result, we currently
do not hold any interests in any Investments and have not generated any revenues. Over the next twelve months, we intend to commence the private offering and begin investment operations. In addition, as described further below, a subsidiary of
Blackstone has agreed to acquire certain investments on behalf of BXHF up to an aggregate invested equity amount of $500 million or such greater amount as mutually agreed between the parties. Further, BXHF has agreed to acquire, and such subsidiary
has agreed to transfer, such investments on the terms described in the Warehousing Agreement (as defined below) following such time as BXHF has sufficient capital to acquire such investments. See &#8220;<I>Item 1A. Risk Factors&#8212;Potential
Conflicts of Interest&#8212;Risks Related to Transactions Under the Warehousing</I><I> Agreement</I>&#8221; for more information. See also &#8220;<I>&#8212;Investment Process Overview</I>&#8221; below for information regarding the Fund&#8217;s
process for identifying, evaluating and monitoring investments. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Overview of Blackstone and Blackstone&#8217;s Multi-Asset Investing Division
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund combines its flexible investment mandate with the scale of Blackstone, the world&#8217;s largest alternative asset manager.
Blackstone&#8217;s size and scope provides valuable data-driven insights, with total assets under management of more than $1.2 trillion and approximately 5,200 employees at our headquarters in New </P>

to engage directly and indirectly through the Underlying Investment Vehicles in hedging transactions for the purpose of efficient portfolio management. The Sponsor will review the hedging policy of BXHF from time to time depending on movements and
projected movements of the relevant currencies and interest rates and the availability of cost-effective hedging instruments for BXHF at the relevant time. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">We will make certain Investments by investing in or alongside Other Blackstone Accounts, subject to the terms and conditions of our and such
Other Blackstone Accounts&#8217; governing documents. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>BXHF Fund Program </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund, Aggregator, any Feeder Vehicles and/or any Parallel Funds (as applicable) together form BXHF, a multi-strategy investment program.
BXHF may invest alongside one or more vehicles with substantially similar investment objectives and strategies (such vehicles as determined in the Investment Manager&#8217;s sole discretion, &#8220;<B>Other Similar Funds</B>&#8221;). While these
Other Similar Funds would be operated as distinct investment structures, they would be expected to have highly overlapping investment portfolios and would together with BXHF form the &#8220;<B>BXHF Fund Program</B>.&#8221; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>The Investment Manager, the General Partner and the Affiliated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Manager </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Fund expects to enter into the investment management agreement (as may be amended, supplemented restated or otherwise modified from time to
time, the &#8220;<B>Investment Management Agreement</B>&#8221;) with Blackstone Alternative Asset Management L.P. (previously defined as the &#8220;<B>Investment Manager</B>&#8221;) and an amended and restated limited partnership agreement (as may
be amended, supplemented restated or otherwise modified from time to time, the &#8220;<B>Partnership Agreement</B>&#8221;), with Blackstone Alternative Asset Management Associates LLC (previously defined as the &#8220;<B>General
Partner</B>&#8221;),<B> </B>pursuant to which the Sponsor will manage the Fund on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> basis. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Overall responsibility for BXHF&#8217;s oversight rests with the General Partner, subject to certain oversight rights held by the Fund&#8217;s
Board of Directors. See &#8220;<I>&#8212;The Board of Directors</I>&#8221; and &#8220;<I>&#8212;Partnership Agreement</I>&#8221; below for further information. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The General Partner will delegate the portfolio management function regarding BXHF to the Investment Manager. The Investment Manager will have
discretion to make Investments on behalf of BXHF. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Investment Manager expects to enter into a
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">sub-investment</FONT> management agreement (as may be amended, supplemented restated or otherwise modified from time to time, the &#8220;<B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Management
Agreement</B>&#8221;) with Blackstone Alternative Solutions L.L.C. (previously defined as the &#8220;<B>Affiliated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Manager</B>&#8221; or &#8220;<B>BAS</B>&#8221; and together with the Investment
Manager, the &#8220;<B>BXHF Managers</B>&#8221;) pursuant to which the Investment Manager expects to delegate the portfolio management function for a portion of BXHF&#8217;s Investments to the Affiliated
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Manager. BXHF will not pay the Affiliated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment&nbsp;Manager</FONT> a separate fee in consideration of its services pursuant to the <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Management Agreement. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Investment Manager, a Delaware limited partnership, and
the Affiliated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Manager, a Delaware limited liability company, each have a business address at 345 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10154, United States of America. Each of the BXHF Managers is
registered with the SEC as an investment adviser under the U.S. Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended from time to time (the &#8220;<B>Advisers Act</B>&#8221;). The BXHF Managers will be responsible for initiating, structuring, and negotiating
BXHF&#8217;s Investments. In addition, the BXHF Managers will actively manage and monitor each Investment, as applicable, to seek to maximize the value of each Investment. </P>

Underlying Managers, BXHF will bear its pro rata share of management fees and performance-based allocations or fees charged or applied by such unaffiliated Underlying Managers in respect of their respective Underlying Investment Vehicles, in
addition to fees charged at the BXHF level (i.e., there will be &#8220;double fees&#8221; involved in making an investment in an Underlying Investment Vehicle through BXHF which would not arise if the Unitholder were to invest in the Underlying
Investment Vehicle directly, because the Sponsor and its affiliates will receive fees with respect to the management of BXHF, on the one hand, and the Underlying Manager will receive additional fees with respect to the management of such Underlying
Investment Vehicles, on the other hand), which will increase the amount of expenses borne by BXHF (and indirectly by Unitholders) and reduce returns. In connection with Investments&nbsp;(a) in Underlying Investment Vehicles or (b)&nbsp;that are
sourced and/or managed, in each case, by Underlying Managers that are affiliated with the BXHF Managers, BXHF is not expected to pay or otherwise bear carried interest, management fees or other incentive compensation that may be otherwise charged or
applied by such affiliated Underlying Managers, except in limited circumstances, in which case such carried interest, management fees or other incentive compensation paid will be rebated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">dollar-for-dollar,</FONT></FONT> or waived to create a single level of fees to the Sponsor, in the General Partner&#8217;s sole discretion. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">BXHF will directly or indirectly bear other expenses in connection with an investment in an Underlying Investment Vehicle, including any
investment related expenses and expenses paid to affiliates of the Sponsor, administrative expenses and other expenses included in the definition of Fund Expenses below as applicable to such Underlying Investment Vehicle (to the extent applicable).

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Management Fee </U> </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In
consideration for its investment management services, the Investment Manager will be entitled to receive a management fee (the &#8220;<B>Management Fee</B>&#8221;) payable by BXHF directly or indirectly through an Intermediate Entity equal to, in
the aggregate, 1.25% of the Aggregator&#8217;s NAV per annum. The Management Fee will be accrued monthly and payable quarterly, before giving effect to any accruals for the Management Fee, the Servicing Fee (as defined below), the Administration Fee
(as defined below), the Performance Participation Allocation (as defined below), pending Aggregator Unit redemptions or distributions, if any, and without taking into account accrued and unpaid taxes of any Intermediate Entity (including
Corporations) through which BXHF indirectly invests in an Investment (or any comparable entities of Other Blackstone Accounts in which BXHF directly or indirectly participates) or taxes paid by any such entity during the applicable month. Each of
the Fund, any Feeder Vehicle and/or any Parallel Fund (as applicable) will bear (without duplication) its proportional share of the Management Fee paid based on its proportional interest in the Aggregator. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Investment Manager may elect to receive the Management Fee in cash, Units of the Fund, units of any Parallel Fund and/or shares, units or
interests (as applicable) of Intermediate Entities (which may, for the avoidance of doubt, be paid or allocated directly by an Intermediate Entity). If the Management Fee is paid in Units, such Units may be redeemed quarterly at the Investment
Manager&#8217;s request and will be subject to the volume limitations of the Unit Redemption Plan but not the Early Redemption Deduction. Additionally, the Investment Manager may separately elect for the Management Fee to be paid (in whole or in
part) to an affiliate of the Investment Manager in satisfaction of Management Fee amounts owed to the Investment Manager in connection with services provided by such affiliate to BXHF and/or any Intermediate Entity. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Performance Participation Allocation </U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The General Partner<B> </B>will be allocated a performance participation (the &#8220;<B>Performance Participation Allocation</B>&#8221;) by
BXHF directly or indirectly through an Intermediate Entity equal to 12.5% of Total Return subject to a 5% annual Hurdle Amount and a High Water Mark with 100% <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Catch-Up</FONT> (each as defined below). Such allocation
will be measured on a calendar year basis, be paid quarterly and accrued monthly (subject to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pro-rating</FONT> for partial periods). For the first calendar year of the Fund&#8217;s operations the allocation will be
paid at the end of such first calendar year and thereafter the allocation will be paid quarterly. Each of the Fund, any Feeder Vehicle and/or any Parallel Fund (as applicable) will bear (without duplication) its proportional share of the Performance
Participation Allocation based on its proportional interest in the Aggregator. For further information regarding the Performance Participation Allocation (as defined herein), see &#8220;<I>Item 2. Financial Information&#8212;Management&#8217;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8212;Expenses&#8212;Performance Participation Allocation</I>&#8221; below. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">BXHF expects to benefit from an investment committee that is composed of some of the most senior and experienced investment professionals at
Blackstone (the &#8220;<B>BXHF Investment Committee</B>&#8221;), including, as of the date of this Registration Statement, Jonathan Gray (President and COO of Blackstone), Michael Chae (CFO and Vice Chairman of Blackstone), Kenneth Caplan (Global
Co-CIO of Blackstone), Joe Dowling (Global Head of BXMA), Riad Abrahams (Director and CEO of BXHF), Ravi Desai (President of BXHF), Atish Nigam (CIO of BXMA Multi-Strategy Platform), David Ben-Ur (CIO of BXMA Absolute Return Platform) and Farhad
Karim (COO of Blackstone Private Wealth and Director of BXHF). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The BXHF Investment Committee&#8217;s primary responsibility will be to
determine allocations across the Fund&#8217;s strategies. The BXHF Investment Committee will rely upon the decisions of, or delegate approval to, BAS&#8217; investment committee and BXMA&#8217;s Absolute Return investment committee, which in turn
delegate authority to (i)&nbsp;certain authorized principals of the BXHF Managers, including the Chief Investment Officer of the BXMA Multi-Strategy Platform, and/or (ii) Underlying Managers to manage and/or invest certain assets under management on
a discretionary basis. The BXHF Investment Committee may, from time to time, review and approve certain direct Investments as deemed appropriate by the Investment Manager. One or more senior Blackstone employees are expected to generally participate
in Investment Committee meetings as observers. There is significant overlap between BXHF&#8217;s Investment Committee, BAS&#8217; investment committee and BXMA&#8217;s Absolute Return investment committee. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The BXHF Investment Committee will on a regular basis and on an ad hoc basis as it deems necessary or appropriate, review the portfolio and
risk profile of the Investments (including any Investments approved by BAS&#8217; investment committee, BXMA&#8217;s Absolute Return investment committee and/or certain authorized principals of the BXHF Managers). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">BXHF will leverage the various investment, asset management, portfolio operations, finance, and legal and compliance professionals located

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the core of Blackstone&#8217;s investment strategy is a rigorous investment origination,
selection and investment decision process with considerable emphasis on monitoring and reporting the performance of the ongoing investment portfolio. Our investment review and monitoring process&#8212;from the initial identification of an investment
opportunity to the final investment decision, through to ultimate monetization&#8212;is a disciplined approach designed to screen out transactions with excessive risk, actively monitor investments and capitalize on opportunities to generate
attractive, risk-adjusted returns. The following is a general outline of our investment process for investments that are brought to the BXHF Investment Committee (or BAS&#8217; investment committee and/or BXMA&#8217;s Absolute Return investment
committee, as applicable): </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">

include, but are </P>

Blackstone<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">1</SUP> and external service providers to assess any structural, operational, tax, regulatory or other risks associated with the investment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Monitoring / Value Creation </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The BXHF Managers will oversee BXHF&#8217;s portfolio on an ongoing basis. We seek to control risk in a number of ways that may include
diversification across investment strategies, underlying instruments, geography and the expected maturity or holding periods of positions; hedging of foreign exchange, equity beta, interest rate and credit spread exposure; selective use of leverage;
risk analysis; and operational controls. A central element of the Investment Manager&#8217;s risk management effort is its monitoring and reporting process. This process involves conducting frequent reviews of each direct Investment and conducting
meetings and/or calls with representatives of portfolio companies or Underlying Managers in which BXHF directly or indirectly invests. To the extent any Investment is underperforming, the Investment Manager will consider its ability to positively
influence the performance of that Investment, opportunities to mitigate losses, and/or its ability to cause BXHF to exit such Investment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Each strategy and its underlying investments are monitored regularly to account for market-driven and idiosyncratic changes, with the team
continually monitoring the ongoing risk-reward profile. Using proprietary tools, investment teams produce regular updates to keep the senior BXHF leadership informed of position-level developments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Prior to investing BXHF&#8217;s assets with any Underlying Manager, the BXHF Managers and/or their affiliates screen the Underlying Manager
and may establish agreed upon investment guidelines and other terms. In particular, the BXHF Managers generally seek to measure and monitor risks relating to the Investments and the Underlying Managers and their respective Underlying Investment
Vehicles, as applicable. The amount and quality of risk due diligence, measurement and monitoring is dependent on access to the portfolios and risk management systems (if any) of the Underlying Managers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Competition </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">BXHF&#8217;s investment
mandate is highly competitive and involves a high degree of uncertainty. We believe that Blackstone&#8217;s successful track record across multiple asset class investments, the ability to leverage Blackstone&#8217;s global deal sourcing network and
Blackstone&#8217;s ability to navigate complex multi-stakeholder processes provide BXHF with a competitive edge. The Sponsor will compete for the acquisition of Investments with many other investors, some of which may have greater resources than the
Fund. Such competitors may include other investment funds, as well as individuals, financial institutions and other institutions. Further, over the past several years, an ever-increasing number of investment funds have been formed (and many existing
funds have grown in size). Additional funds with similar investment objectives may be formed in the future by other unrelated and/or related parties. The availability of investment opportunities generally will be subject to market conditions, as
well as, in some cases, the prevailing regulatory or political climate. In addition, certain Other Blackstone Accounts that have investment strategies that are adjacent to or overlap with those of the BXHF Fund Program (whether now in existence or
subsequently established). Blackstone and certain Other Blackstone Accounts may share and/or receive priority with respect to certain investment opportunities or receive allocations of investments otherwise appropriate for the BXHF Fund Program
(including, for example, Other Blackstone Accounts advised and/or managed by the Investment Manager or BAS). See <I>&#8220;&#8212;Allocation of Investment Opportunities and Capacity&#8221;</I> for more information of allocations of investments among
the BXHF Fund Program and Other Blackstone Accounts. </P>

distinct investment structures, they are expected to have highly overlapping investment portfolios. As a result, certain conflicts may arise between BXHF and Other Similar Funds with respect to the allocation of investment opportunities. Investment
opportunities will be allocated between BXHF and Other Similar Funds in accordance with Blackstone&#8217;s policies and procedures, which generally provide that allocations are determined on a basis that the Sponsor believes to be fair and
reasonable in its sole discretion, which typically will be pro rata, subject to the following considerations (among others): (a)&nbsp;any applicable investment strategies, mandates, objectives, focus, parameters, guidelines, limitations, liquidity
positions and requirements of BXHF and Other Similar Funds; (b)&nbsp;available capital of BXHF and Other Similar Funds; and (c)&nbsp;legal, tax, accounting, regulatory and any other considerations deemed relevant by the Sponsor, including, without
limitation, the considerations described in &#8220;<I>Item 1A. Risk Factors&#8212;Potential Conflicts of Interest&#8212;Allocation of Investment Opportunities and Capacity.</I>&#8221; </P>

will overlap with the investment strategies of Other Blackstone Accounts that are actively investing and similarly overlap with future Other Blackstone Accounts. In certain circumstances, such Other Blackstone Accounts are expected to have a
priority over the Fund in respect of particular investment opportunities. Blackstone seeks to allocate investment opportunities among the Fund and Other Blackstone Account in a manner that, over time, is on a fair and equitable basis and has
established written allocation policies and procedures to guide the determination of such allocations. If an investment opportunity is appropriate for the BXHF Fund Program and one or more Other Blackstone Accounts, the Investment Manager and/or the
Affiliated <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Sub-Investment</FONT> Manager, as applicable, and Blackstone will determine allocations of such opportunity in their sole discretion in accordance with such written allocation policies and procedures,
taking into account various criteria, including, but not limited to: available capacity; targeted investment/sale size; investment strategies, target returns, objectives and time horizon; the extent of involvement of the respective teams of
investment professionals dedicated to the respective clients in sourcing and underwriting the investment; legal and regulatory restrictions; investment guidelines/restrictions; investment liquidity levels; available capital; fund/relationship size;
investment type, geographic focus, asset class, sector and anticipated hold period; the relative risk/return profile of the investment; relation to existing investments in a fund or client account, if applicable (e.g., &#8220;follow on&#8221; to
existing investment or same security as existing investment); </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">BXHF may utilize leverage, incur indebtedness and provide other credit support for any purpose, including to fund all or a portion of the

the exercise of rights attached to an investment). Additionally, BXHF may incur additional indebtedness for borrowed money that causes the Leverage Ratio to exceed 30% to the extent (a)&nbsp;the General Partner expects at the time of each such
incurrence that the Leverage Ratio shall be reduced to less than or equal to 30% within nine months from the date the Leverage Ratio initially exceeded 30% and (b)&nbsp;a majority of the Independent Directors approve such additional indebtedness as
being in the best interests of BXHF. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>&#8220;Leverage Ratio&#8221; </B>means, on any date of incurrence of any such indebtedness, the
quotient obtained by dividing (a)&nbsp;Aggregate Net Leverage (as defined below) by (b)&nbsp;the aggregate <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">month-end</FONT> values of BXHF&#8217;s Investments, plus the value of any other assets (such as cash on
hand), as determined in accordance with BXHF&#8217;s Valuation Policy. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>&#8220;Aggregate Net Leverage&#8221; </B>means (a)&nbsp;the
aggregate amount of recourse indebtedness for borrowed money (e.g., bank debt) of BXHF minus (b)&nbsp;cash and cash equivalents of BXHF minus, without duplication, (c)&nbsp;cash used in connection with funding a deposit in advance of the closing of
an Investment and working capital advances. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For purposes of determining Aggregate Net Leverage, the General Partner shall use the
principal amount of borrowings, and not the valuations of BXHF&#8217;s borrowings, and may, in its sole discretion, determine which securities and other instruments are deemed to be cash equivalents. BXHF&#8217;s assets or any part thereof,
including any accounts of BXHF, may be pledged in connection with any credit facilities or borrowings. For the avoidance of doubt, the Leverage Limit does not apply to (i)&nbsp;indebtedness incurred by an Intermediate Entity (including, for the
avoidance of doubt, the Aggregator) or Portfolio Entity that is <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-recourse</FONT> to the Fund,&nbsp;(ii) refinancings of </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The SEC adopted Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">206(4)-6</FONT> under the Advisers Act, which requires registered investment advisors
that exercise voting authority over client securities to implement proxy voting policies. In compliance with such rule, the Investment Manager has adopted proxy voting policies and procedures. Underlying Managers also are expected to adopt and
implement proxy voting policies and procedures that comply with the requirements of Rule <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">206(4)-6,</FONT> and generally will be responsible for exercising voting discretion over proxies with respect to the securities
they manage. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the case of Investments which are not managed by an Underlying Manager, the Investment Manager expects to engage the
services of a third-party service provider to make recommendations to the Investment Manager on the voting of proxies related to such securities. Such third party provides voting recommendations based on established guidelines and practices. The
Investment Manager generally will vote proxies in accordance with such third party&#8217;s recommendations, but may decide not to vote in accordance with the third party&#8217;s recommendations if it believes that the specific recommendation is not
in the best interests of the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the case of interests held by the Fund in pooled vehicles, the general policy is for the Investment
Manager to vote proxy proposals submitted to investors in such pooled vehicles in a manner that serves the best interests of the Fund, determined by the Investment Manager in its discretion. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>The discussion of tax matters set forth in this Registration Statement was not intended to be used, and cannot be used by any prospective

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This summary discusses certain U.S. federal income tax considerations relating to an investment in Units of BXHF. This discussion is based on
provisions of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;<B>Code</B>&#8221;), on the regulations promulgated thereunder, and on published administrative rulings and judicial decisions now in effect, all of which are subject to
change or different interpretation, possibly with retroactive effect. This discussion is necessarily general and may not apply to all categories of investors, some of which, such as banks, thrifts, insurance companies, dealers and other investors
that do not own their Units as capital assets and investors required to accelerate the recognition of any item of gross income with respect to the Fund or its investments as a result of such income being recognized on an applicable financial
statement, may be subject to special rules. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholders and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> Unitholders (as defined below) are discussed separately below. The actual tax
consequences of the purchase and ownership of Units in BXHF will vary depending upon the investor&#8217;s circumstances. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For purposes
of this discussion, a &#8220;<B>U.S. Person</B>&#8221; or a &#8220;<B>U.S. Unitholder</B>&#8221; is an individual who is a citizen or resident of the United States, as determined for U.S. federal income tax purposes, a corporation or an entity
treated as a corporation for such purposes that is created or organized in or under the laws of the United States, any state thereof or the District of Columbia, an estate, the income of which is subject to U.S. federal income taxation regardless of
its source, or a trust if (1)&nbsp;it is subject to the primary supervision of a court within the United States and one or more U.S. Persons have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust, or (2)&nbsp;it has a valid election in
effect under applicable Treasury Regulations to be treated as a U.S. Person. A &#8220;<B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> Person</B>&#8221; is a person that is not a U.S. Person, and a
&#8220;<B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> Unitholder</B>&#8221; is a Unitholder (other than a partnership) that is not a U.S. Person. The Fund will make investments through BXHF SPV (CYM) L.P., a non-U.S. Corporation that will
invest all or substantially all of its assets in the Aggregator. The &#8220;<B>Cayman Fund</B>&#8221; shall mean BXHF Offshore Feeder L.P., a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership entity formed by the General Partner in order to mitigate the
uncertainty of the imposition of U.S. federal estate tax on the estate of an individual <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> Unitholder. The Cayman Fund is expected to be treated as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes and
will invest all or substantially all of its assets in the Aggregator. An investment in the </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If a partnership (or an entity treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes) holds Units, the tax treatment of a partner will

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B></B><B><I>Partnership Status</I></B><B>. Subject to the discussion of &#8220;publicly traded partnerships&#8221; set forth below, a
domestic business entity (such as the Fund) that has two or more members and that is not organized as a corporation under federal or state law will generally be classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The classification of
an entity as a partnership for such purposes may not be respected for state or local tax purposes. </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">An entity that would otherwise be
classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes may nonetheless be taxable as a corporation if it is a &#8220;publicly traded partnership.&#8221; An exception, referred to as the &#8220;<B>Qualifying Income Exception</B>,&#8221;
exists with respect to a publicly traded partnership if (i)&nbsp;at least 90% of such partnership&#8217;s gross income for every taxable year consists of &#8220;qualifying income&#8221; and (ii)&nbsp;the partnership would not be required to register
under the 1940 Act if it were a U.S. corporation. Qualifying income includes certain interest income, dividends, real property rents, gains from the sale or other disposition of real property, and any gain from the sale or disposition of a capital
asset or other property held for the production of income that otherwise constitutes qualifying income. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The General Partner intends
to manage the affairs of the Fund so that it will either (i)&nbsp;not be treated as a &#8220;publicly traded partnership&#8221; or (ii)&nbsp;meet the Qualifying Income Exception in each taxable year. However, the portion of the Fund&#8217;s income
that is qualifying income may change from time to time, and there can be no assurance that at least 90% of the Fund&#8217;s gross income in any year will constitute qualifying income. No ruling has been or will be sought from the Internal Revenue
Service (the &#8220;<B>IRS</B>&#8221;), and there can be no assurance that the IRS will not attempt to recharacterize the Fund as an association or publicly traded partnership taxable as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes. If the
Fund is determined to be taxable as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes, it would be taxable on its earnings at the corporate income tax rate and any distributions to the partners would be taxable as dividends to the Unitholders to
the extent of the earnings and profits of the Fund. In any event, significant amounts of the assets of the Fund and the Cayman Fund are expected to be held through entities taxable as corporations for U.S. federal income tax purposes and some
corporations are expected to be subject to U.S. corporate federal (and applicable state and local) income tax. The remainder of this discussion assumes that the Fund will be treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B><I>Taxation of U.S. Unitholders </I></B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Each U.S. Unitholder will be required to take into account, as described below, its distributive share of each item of the Fund&#8217;s income,
gain, loss, deduction, and credit for each taxable year of the Fund ending with or within the U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s taxable year. See &#8220;<I>&#8212;Allocations of Income, Gain, Loss, and Deduction</I>&#8221; below. Generally, each item will
have the same character and the same source (either U.S. or foreign), as though the U.S. Unitholder realized the item directly. U.S. Unitholders must report those items regardless of the extent to which, or whether, they receive cash distributions
from the Fund for such taxable year. Moreover, the Fund may invest (directly or indirectly) in certain securities, such as original issue discount obligations or preferred stock </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Medicare Tax</U><I>. </I>U.S. Unitholders that are individuals, estates, or trusts are subject to a Medicare tax of 3.8% on &#8220;net
investment income&#8221; (or undistributed &#8220;net investment income,&#8221; in the case of estates and trusts) for each taxable year, with such tax applying to the lesser of such income or the excess of such person&#8217;s adjusted gross income
(with certain adjustments) over a specified amount. Net investment income includes net income from interest, dividends, annuities, royalties, rents, and net gain attributable to the disposition of investment property. It is anticipated that net
income and gain attributable to an investment in the Fund will be included in a U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s &#8220;net investment income&#8221; subject to this Medicare tax. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Fund Distributions</U><I>. </I>Distributions of cash (including, in certain circumstances, distributions of certain &#8220;marketable
securities&#8221; treated as cash distributions) from the Fund to a U.S. Unitholder in any year will reduce the adjusted basis of the U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s partnership interest by the amount of such cash distribution. To the extent such
distributions exceed the adjusted basis of a U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s partnership interest, such U.S. Unitholder will be treated as having recognized gain from the sale or exchange of such interest. In general, distributions (other than liquidating
distributions) of property other than cash will reduce the adjusted basis (but not below zero) of a U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s partnership interest by the amount of the partnership&#8217;s adjusted basis in such property immediately before its
distribution but will not result in the realization of taxable income to the Unitholder. For these purposes, a reduction in a U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s share of the Fund&#8217;s debt, including when a new Unitholder is admitted to the Fund, will
result in a deemed cash distribution to the Unitholder in an amount equal to the reduction. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Basis</U><I>. </I>A U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s adjusted basis in its partnership interest
is, in general, equal to the amount of cash the U.S. Unitholder has contributed to the Fund, increased by the U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s share of income and liabilities of the Fund and decreased by the U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s proportionate share of
cash distributions, losses, and reductions in such liabilities. Each U.S. Unitholder will (subject to certain limits discussed below) be entitled to deduct its allocable share of the Fund losses to the extent of its tax basis in its Interest at the
end of the tax year of the Fund in which such losses are recognized. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Allocations of Income, Gain, Loss, and Deduction</U><I>.
</I>Pursuant to the Partnership Agreement, items of the Fund&#8217;s income, gain, loss, and deduction are allocated so as to take into account the varying interests of the Unitholders in the Fund. Treasury Regulations provide that allocations of
items of partnership income, gain, loss, deduction, or credit will be respected for tax purposes if such allocations have &#8220;substantial economic effect&#8221; or are determined to be in accordance with the partners&#8217; interests in a
partnership. The Fund believes that, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, allocations pursuant to the Partnership Agreement should be given effect, and the General Partner intends to prepare tax information returns based on such allocations. If the
IRS were to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">re-determine</FONT> the allocations to a particular U.S. Unitholder, such redetermination could be less favorable than the allocations set forth in the Partnership Agreement. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Deduction for Certain Qualified Business Income and Certain REIT Dividends</U>. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-corporate</FONT>
taxpayers may be allowed a deduction of 20% of certain domestic business income (excluding capital gains, dividend income, and certain types of compensation) received from partnerships engaged in business other than specified service businesses
(i.e., businesses in the fields of law, health, accounting, financial services, brokerage services, or businesses where the principal asset of the business is the reputation or skill of its employees or owners or businesses which involve the
performance of services consisting of investing and investment management). A high income taxpayer&#8217;s deduction is limited to the greater of (a) 50% of its <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pro-rata</FONT> share of
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-2</FONT> wages paid by such partnership, or (b)&nbsp;the sum of 25% of such <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">W-2</FONT> wages plus 2.5% of the tax basis of certain depreciable property used in the trade or
business. Ordinary dividends from real estate investment trusts (&#8220;<B>REITs</B>&#8221;) and certain allocations from publicly traded partnerships may also benefit from the 20% deduction, without the foregoing limitations. A substantial amount
of income of BXHF may not be eligible for the deduction. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Limitations on Deductions</U><I>. </I>While the Fund is not intended as a
&#8220;tax shelter,&#8221; it is possible that losses and expenses could exceed the Fund&#8217;s income and gain in a given year. The ability of a Unitholder to deduct such a net loss from its taxable income from other sources may be subject to a
number of limitations under the Code. For example, each U.S. Unitholder will not be entitled to deduct its share of the Fund&#8217;s losses in excess of its tax basis at the end of the tax year of the Fund in which such losses are recognized. Other
limitations include the limitation on <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;tax-exempt</FONT> use loss&#8221; under Section&nbsp;470 of the Code, and for certain investors, such as individuals, the &#8220;at risk&#8221; rules of Section&nbsp;465
of the Code and the disallowance of miscellaneous itemized deductions under Section&nbsp;67 of the Code, limitations on interest deductions under Section&nbsp;163 of the Code, and the limitations on passive activity losses of Section&nbsp;469 of the
Code. Because of some of those limitations, it is possible that, if the Fund has losses and income from different types of activities, certain investors may not be able to use losses from the Fund to reduce income therefrom. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Organization, Management and Syndication Expenses</U><I>. </I>In general, neither the Fund nor any Unitholder may deduct organization or
syndication expenses. An election may be made by a partnership to amortize organizational expenses over a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">180-month</FONT> period, although the Fund does not intend to make such election. Syndication fees (which
would include any sales or placement fees or commissions), however, must be capitalized and cannot be amortized or otherwise deducted. The Management Fees paid to the Investment Manager (and similar fees paid to the investment advisers of the
underlying investment funds in which the Fund holds interests) may not be deductible (or if deductible, may be subject to limitations on deductibility). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Limitations on Deduction of Business Interest</U><I>. </I>Deductions for business interest expense (even if paid to third parties) in
excess of the sum of a taxpayer&#8217;s business interest income and 30% of the adjusted taxable income of the business, which is its taxable income computed without regard to business interest income or
</P>

a trade or business, but excludes investment interest, to which separate limitations apply.<I> </I> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Sale or Disposition of BXHF
Units</U><I>. </I>A U.S. Unitholder that sells or otherwise disposes of an interest in the Fund in a taxable transaction generally will recognize gain or loss equal to the difference, if any, between the adjusted basis of the interest and the amount
realized from the sale or disposition. The amount realized will include the Unitholder&#8217;s share of the Fund&#8217;s liabilities outstanding at the time of the sale or disposition. If the Unitholder holds the interest as a capital asset, such
gain or loss will generally be treated as capital gain or loss to the extent a sale of assets by the Fund would qualify for such treatment and will generally be long-term capital gain or loss if the Unitholder had held the interest for more than one
year on the date of such sale or disposition, provided, that a capital contribution by the Unitholder within the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-year</FONT> period ending on such date will cause part of such gain or loss to be short-term. In
addition, if the capital contribution of a new Unitholder is distributed to the Unitholders (other than such new Unitholder), for U.S. federal income tax purposes such distributions may be treated as a taxable sale of a portion of their interests by
Unitholders receiving such distributions. In the event of a sale or other transfer of an interest at any time other than the end of the Fund&#8217;s taxable year, the share of income and losses of the Fund for the year of transfer attributable to
the interest transferred will be allocated for U.S. federal income tax purposes between the transferor and the transferee on an interim
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">closing-of-the-books</FONT></FONT></FONT> basis, pro rata basis, or other reasonable method determined by the General Partner reflecting the
respective periods during such year that each of the transferor and the transferee owned the interest. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Foreign Tax Credit
Limitations</U><I>. </I>U.S. Unitholders may be entitled to a foreign tax credit with respect to creditable foreign taxes paid on the income and gains of the Fund (or from such Unitholder&#8217;s share of income and gains of an investment fund in
which the Fund holds interests). Complex rules may, however, depending on each U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s circumstances, limit the availability or use of foreign tax credits. In particular, gain recognized on the sale of a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> investment will generally be treated as U.S. source gain with respect to a U.S. Unitholder for foreign tax credit purposes and therefore a U.S. Unitholder may not be able to claim a credit for any foreign
taxes imposed upon such sale unless such credit can be applied against tax due on other income treated as derived from foreign sources. Further, U.S. Unitholders will generally not be entitled to an indirect foreign tax credit with respect to
foreign taxes paid by an entity in which the Fund invests that is treated as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Capital gains realized by the Fund may be considered to be from sources within the U.S., which may effectively limit the
amount of foreign tax credit allowed to the U.S. Unitholder. In addition, Treasury Regulations that apply to taxes paid or accrued in taxable years beginning on or after December&nbsp;28, 2021 impose additional requirements for foreign taxes to be
eligible for a foreign tax credit (the &#8220;<B>Foreign Tax Credit Regulations</B>&#8221;). The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the IRS are considering proposing amendments to the Foreign Tax Credit Regulations. In addition, recent notices from
the IRS provide temporary relief by allowing taxpayers that comply with applicable requirements to apply many aspects of the foreign tax credit regulations as they previously existed (before the release of the Foreign Tax Credit Regulations) for
taxable years ending before the date that a notice or other guidance withdrawing or modifying the temporary relief is issued (or any later date specified in such notice or other guidance). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Instead of claiming a foreign tax credit, a U.S. Unitholder may be able to deduct foreign taxes on its share of gain from the sale of the
Fund&#8217;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> investments in computing its taxable income, subject to generally applicable limitations under United States law (including that a U.S. holder is not eligible for a deduction for foreign
income taxes paid or accrued in a taxable year if such U.S. holder claims a foreign tax credit for any foreign income taxes paid or accrued in the same taxable year). Certain losses arising from the Fund may be treated as foreign source losses,
which could reduce the amount of foreign tax credits otherwise available. U.S. Unitholders should consult with their individual tax advisors regarding the availability of the foreign tax credit (or a deduction in lieu of such credit) under their
particular circumstances. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> Currency Gain or Loss</U><I>. </I>The Fund may engage in
transactions involving <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> currencies, including <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> currency hedging transactions, and the Fund and the U.S. Unitholders may experience foreign

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Issues Relating to Foreign Corporations</U><I>. </I>U.S. Unitholders may be subject to special rules applicable to indirect investments in
foreign corporations, including those discussed below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Controlled Foreign Corporations</U>. If a U.S. Person, including any U.S.
Unitholder, owns actually or constructively at least 10% of the voting stock or value of a foreign corporation, such U.S. Person is considered a &#8220;United States Shareholder&#8221; with respect to the foreign corporation. If United States
Shareholders in the aggregate own more than 50% of the voting power or value of the stock of such corporation, the foreign corporation will be classified as a &#8220;controlled foreign corporation&#8221; (a &#8220;<B>CFC</B>&#8221;). For this
purpose, each <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> investment fund in which the Fund invests generally will be regarded as transparent, and the Fund will be deemed to own its proportionate share of any stock of a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> corporation that is owned directly or indirectly by such <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> investment fund. If the Fund or a U.S. investment fund in which the Fund invests, as the case may
be, owns an interest in a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> corporation, the Fund or such U.S. investment fund, as the case may be, will be treated as a United States Shareholder of any <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT>
corporation in which its share ownership reaches this 10% threshold. If the corporation qualifies as a CFC at any time during the taxable year, the United States Shareholders of the CFC may be subject to current U.S. tax on certain types of income
of the foreign corporation (e.g., dividends, interest, certain rents and royalties, gain from the sale of property producing such income, certain income from sales and services and certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">low-taxed</FONT> foreign
income), regardless of cash distributions from the CFC. In addition, gain on the sale of the CFC&#8217;s stock by a United States Shareholder (during the period that the corporation is a CFC and thereafter for a five-year period) would be classified
in whole or in part as a dividend. It is possible that one or more of the foreign corporations in which the Fund invests (directly or indirectly) may be classified as CFCs and that the Fund or an investment fund in which the Fund invests may be
treated as a United States Shareholder. Proposed regulations would allow U.S. Persons to look through the Fund for purposes of determining any current inclusions under the CFC rules, but would still require a portion of gain on sale to be classified
in whole or in part as dividend income. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Passive Foreign Investment Companies</U>. The Fund is expected to hold its interests in
the Aggregator and make a significant portion of its acquisitions, including U.S. acquisitions, through one or more <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> Corporations which would be expected to be &#8220;passive foreign investment
companies&#8221; (&#8220;<B>PFICs</B>&#8221;). U.S. Unitholders may be subject to special rules under U.S. tax law dealing with PFICs. A PFIC is defined as any foreign corporation in which either (i) 75% or more of its gross income for the taxable
year is &#8220;passive income&#8221; or (ii) 50% or more of its assets in any taxable year (by value) produce &#8220;passive income.&#8221; There are no minimum stock ownership requirements for PFICs. Once a corporation qualifies as a PFIC with
respect to a U.S. shareholder, it is treated as a PFIC with respect to such shareholder for any subsequent taxable year during which such shareholder continues to hold an interest in the corporation, regardless of whether it satisfies either of the
qualification tests in subsequent years, unless an exception applies. Subject to certain exceptions described below, any gain on disposition of stock of the PFIC as well as income realized on certain &#8220;excess distributions&#8221; by the PFIC,
would be treated as though realized ratably over the shorter of a U.S. Unitholder&#8217;s holding period of its Units or the Fund&#8217;s holding period for the PFIC. Such gain or income would be taxed as ordinary income, and dividends paid by the
PFIC would not be eligible for the preferential tax rates for dividends paid to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-corporate</FONT> U.S. Unitholders. In addition, an interest charge would be imposed on the U.S. Unitholder based on the tax treated
as deferred from prior years. To the extent reasonably practicable and administratively feasible, we may structure acquisitions of foreign corporations to avoid holding a PFIC. However, the Fund is expected to hold its investments through an entity
that is expected to be treated as a PFIC. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If the Fund or a U.S. Unitholder were to elect to treat their interest in a PFIC as a
&#8220;qualified electing fund&#8221; (a &#8220;<B>QEF</B>&#8221;) under the Code for the first year they were treated as holding such interest, then in lieu of the foregoing treatment, such U.S. Unitholder would be required to include in income
each year a portion of the ordinary earnings and net capital gains of the qualified fund, even if not distributed to the Fund or the </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Treasury Regulations under Section&nbsp;1411 of the Code contain special rules for applying the 3.8% Medicare tax (as described above under

investors should consult their own tax advisor regarding the implications of the special election, as well as the other implications of the 3.8% Medicare tax and the Treasury Regulations under Section&nbsp;1411 of the Code for their ownership and

the end of the taxable year over the Fund&#8217;s adjusted basis and will be permitted an ordinary loss deduction in respect of the excess, if any, of the adjusted basis of the stock over its fair market value at the end of the taxable year (but
only to the extent of the net amount previously included in income as a result of the election). Prospective investors should consult their own tax advisor regarding the availability of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT

STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> financial accounts worth more than $10,000 at any time during the year. The FBAR regulations continue to reserve on the application of the FBAR rules to ownership by a U.S. Person of an interest in a

possible any such U.S. Unitholders would also be subject to the FBAR filing requirements. Prospective investors should discuss the application of the above rules with their own advisors in light of their individual circumstances. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Separately, under Treasury Regulations, certain U.S. persons that transfer property (including cash) to a

income tax purposes (a &#8220;<B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Recognition</FONT> Transfer</B>&#8221;) are required to file an information report with respect to such transfer with their tax returns, including the filing of IRS Form 926. To

period ending on the date of the transfer exceeds $100,000 (any of (i)&nbsp;or (ii), a &#8220;<B>Cash Contribution Condition</B>&#8221;). To the extent any such transfer is made by a U.S. entity treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax
purposes, the foregoing requirements and determinations are made at the level of any U.S. persons that are partners in such partnership, based on their proportionate ownership interest in such partnership. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Tax-Exempt</FONT> Investors</U><I>. </I>Qualified pension, profit-sharing and stock bonus plans,
educational institutions, and other <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> entities (including private foundations as discussed below) are generally subject to U.S. federal income taxation on their &#8220;unrelated business taxable
income&#8221; (&#8220;<B>UBTI</B>&#8221;). Subject to certain exceptions described below, UBTI is defined as the gross income derived by such a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> entity from an unrelated trade or business (including
a trade or business conducted by a partnership of which the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> entity is a partner), less the deductions directly connected with that trade or business. UBTI generally does not include dividends,
interest, certain types of rents from real property, and gain or loss derived from the sale of property (other than gain or loss derived from the sale of inventory and property sold to customers in the ordinary course of a trade or business). UBTI
does include operating income from certain asset categories owned directly or through entities treated as transparent for U.S. federal income tax purposes. In addition, fee income actually received or deemed to be received by the Fund or the
Unitholders (including any fee income that might be deemed to be received because, although paid to the Investment Manager, or its affiliates, such income results in a reduction in the Management Fee) may be treated as UBTI in certain circumstances.
The Fund intends to take the position that Unitholders do not share in fee income by virtue of such a reduction in Management Fee. The IRS may take a contrary view, however. If that view were ultimately sustained,
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> U.S. Unitholders could be required to pay U.S. federal income tax on that income as UBTI. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> entity&#8217;s acquisition of an interest in a partnership is debt-financed, or a
partnership incurs &#8220;acquisition indebtedness&#8221; that is allocated to the acquisition of a partnership investment, then UBTI may include a percentage of gross income (less the same percentage of deductions) derived from such investment
regardless of whether such income would otherwise be excluded as dividends, interest, rents, gain or loss from sale of eligible property, or similar income. If an entity treated as a flow-through entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes, such as
the Fund, incurs acquisition indebtedness, a U.S. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholder in such flow-through entity (including one holding through a flow-through structure) will be deemed to have acquisition indebtedness
equal to its allocable portion of such acquisition indebtedness, which could generate UBTI for U.S. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholders (given that generally debt incurred by a partnership is attributed to its partners).
If any such indebtedness were used by the Fund (or deemed to be used) to acquire property, such property generally would constitute debt-financed property, and any income from or gain from the disposition of such debt-financed property allocated to
a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> organization (including a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> account) generally would constitute UBTI to such <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> organization,
subject to certain exceptions in cases where debt is paid off. In addition, even if such indebtedness were not used (or deemed to be used) by the Fund to acquire property but were instead used to fund distributions to shareholders, if a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> organization (including a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> account) subject to taxation in the United States were to use such proceeds to make an investment outside the Fund, the IRS
might assert that such investment constitutes debt-financed property to such shareholder with the consequences noted above. The Fund is not prohibited from incurring indebtedness, and no assurance can be provided that the Fund will not generate UBTI
attributable to debt-financed property in the future. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the Fund or the entities through which it invests may earn
operating income that would be UBTI if earned by a U.S. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholder directly. Due to the anticipated operations of the Fund, it is not expected that the Fund will incur income treated as UBTI. In
addition, U.S. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholders are not </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">25 </P>

</DIV></Center>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
permitted to offset losses from one trade or business against the income or gain from another trade or business (even if those trades or businesses are both conducted by the Fund). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In order to mitigate the incurrence of UBTI for U.S. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> investors, the Fund is expected to
incur debt at or below a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> Corporation in which the Fund invests and in which the Fund is expected to hold investments. As a result, investors that invest through the Fund will generally derive returns
from such investments in the form of dividends or capital gain, which are generally excluded from UBTI so long as such investors&#8217; acquisition of interests in the Fund is not debt-financed. Moreover, debt incurred by or below such non-U.S.
Corporation would generally be allocated to such non-U.S. Corporation and not to U.S. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholders. Although it is possible that the IRS could seek to disregard a Corporation through which the Fund
invests and apply the debt-financed property or other UBTI rules to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> investors, the Fund believes such treatment should not apply. A <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> investor is
generally not expected to incur UBTI solely by reason of an investment in the Fund. Each <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> investor is urged to consult with its own tax counsel as to the U.S. federal income tax consequences as a
result of incurring UBTI. </P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> Corporation through which the Fund invests will
generally be subject to the U.S. federal income tax treatment described below under &#8220;<I>&#8212;Taxation of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</FONT> Unitholders</I>.&#8221; Thus, gains from the sale of stock or securities generally are
not subject to U.S. federal income tax and the exemption of interest income under the portfolio interest rules would apply to a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</FONT> Corporation to the extent so described below. However, dividends and
effectively connected income (including gains from the sale of United States real property interest) are subject to U.S. federal income tax. Significant amounts of the assets of the Fund are expected to be held through one or more Corporations and
significant incremental tax may be incurred from the use of such Corporations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If a U.S.
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholder is not otherwise taxable under the UBTI provisions with respect to its Units in the Fund (for example, as debt-financed income), it would not generally be subject to tax under the PFIC
rules or the CFC rules. U.S. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholders should consult their own tax advisors as to the application of the above rules to their particular situations. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Certain Issues Pertaining to Private Foundations</U><I>.</I> In some instances, an investment in the Fund by a private foundation could be
subject to an excise tax to the extent that it constitutes an &#8220;excess business holding&#8221; within the meaning of the Code. For example, if a private foundation (either directly or after taking into account the holdings of its disqualified
persons) acquires more than 20% of the profits interest of the Fund (or 35%, if the private foundation does not directly or indirectly &#8220;control&#8221; the Fund), the private foundation may be considered to have an excess business holding
unless at least 95% of the Fund&#8217;s gross income is from passive sources within the meaning of Section&nbsp;4943(d)(3)(B) of the Code and the private foundation does not own, through the Fund, an excess amount of the voting stock or equivalent
in any business enterprise owned by the Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additionally, if a private foundation generates a substantial amount of UBTI, it may risk
losing its <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> status. Private foundations should consult their own tax advisors regarding the excess business holdings provisions and all other aspects of Chapter 42 of the Code as they relate to an
investment in the Fund, including the level of UBTI that a private foundation may generate as a result of an investment in the Fund. Private foundations should consult their own tax advisors regarding the tax consequences of an investment in the
Fund. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Certain <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> investors may be subject to an excise tax if the Fund engages in a
&#8220;prohibited tax shelter transaction&#8221; or a &#8220;subsequently listed transaction&#8221; within the meaning of Section&nbsp;4965 of the Code. In addition, if the Fund engages in a &#8220;prohibited tax shelter transaction,&#8221; <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> investors may be subject to substantial penalties if they fail to comply with special disclosure requirements and managers of such <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> investors may also be
subject to substantial penalties. Although the Fund does not expect to engage in any such transaction, the rules are subject to interpretation and therefore there can be no assurance that the rules of Section&nbsp;4965 of the Code will not apply to
a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholder. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Tax-exempt</FONT> Unitholders should consult their own tax advisors regarding these rules. </P>
